title: System and Method for Human-Approved Deterministic Finality of Probabilistic Agent Actions via Consensus Gating, Shape-Sum Verification, and Post-Quantum Commitment — U.S. Provisional Patent Application 64/174,202 (Public Filing Notice)
description:
Public filing notice for U.S. Provisional Patent Application 64/174,202, filed October 11, 2026 (priority date secured).

Title: SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR HUMAN-APPROVED DETERMINISTIC FINALITY OF PROBABILISTIC AGENT ACTIONS VIA CONSENSUS GATING, SHAPE-SUM VERIFICATION, AND POST-QUANTUM COMMITMENT

Inventor: Leon Calvin Long II (Briarcliff, Texas, US), inventor-owned.

Abstract: This invention addresses the gap between probabilistic AI agent behavior and deterministic business requirements. It provides a governance envelope in which actions proposed by probabilistic agents attain deterministic finality only after passing: (1) consensus gating across independent verification paths; (2) shape-sum verification of the action's structural fingerprint; and (3) post-quantum cryptographic commitment using approved PQC algorithms; with a human-approval step required before finality for operations of elevated consequence. The result is a system and method by which non-deterministic intelligence can operate inside auditable, deterministic control boundaries, with a verifiable audit trail for every committed action.

SQUIRL OS RESEARCH DISCLOSURE — READ FIRST: This record is part of the Squirl OS research corpus and points at the public GitHub ledger (https://github.com/LLong2026) for implementation material. This disclosure is released under the patent-then-publish doctrine: the corresponding U.S. provisional application was filed and the priority date secured before this public release.

Related public materials: Master thesis monograph "Deterministic Containment of Probabilistic Intelligence: The Squirl OS Journey" (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23303240); Dual Mesh Benchmark paper (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23303081).

This software is a prototype and is provided for educational and research purposes only. It is not intended for production use, commercial deployment, or safety-critical environments. All systems are experimental and may contain defects on them.

Patent note: Priority date October 11, 2026. Application 64/174,202.
